import Mathlib

theorem putnam_2018_a1
  (a b : ℤ)
  (h : 0 < a ∧ 0 < b) :
  ((1 : ℚ) / a + (1 : ℚ) / b = (3 : ℚ) / 2018) ↔
    (⟨a, b⟩ ∈ ({(673, 1358114), (674, 340033), (1009, 2018),
      (2018, 1009), (340033, 674), (1358114, 673)} : Set (ℤ × ℤ))) := by
  constructor
  · -- Forward direction: if the equation holds, then (a,b) is in the set
    intro h_eq
    have h_pos_a : 0 < a := h.1
    have h_pos_b : 0 < b := h.2
    -- Transform the equation: 1/a + 1/b = 3/2018
    -- Multiply by ab*2018: 2018(b+a) = 3ab
    -- Rearrange: 3ab - 2018a - 2018b = 0
    -- Add 2018²/3: (3a - 2018)(3b - 2018) = 2018²
    -- Since 2018 = 2 * 1009 and 1009 is prime, 2018² = 4 * 1009²
    -- We need to find all factorizations of 2018²
    have h₁ : (3 * a - 2018) * (3 * b - 2018) = 2018 ^ 2 := by
      field_simp [h_pos_a.ne', h_pos_b.ne'] at h_eq
      ring_nf at h_eq ⊢
      norm_cast at h_eq ⊢
      linarith
    -- Now enumerate all possible values for (3a - 2018) and (3b - 2018)
    -- These must be divisors of 2018² = 4 * 1009²
    -- Since a, b > 0, we need 3a - 2018 > -2018 and 3b - 2018 > -2018
    -- Also since 1/a + 1/b = 3/2018 > 0, both a and b must be positive
    -- This constrains which divisors are valid
    -- Check each case to see which gives valid integer solutions
    have h₂ : a = 673 ∨ a = 674 ∨ a = 1009 ∨ a = 2018 ∨ a = 340033 ∨ a = 1358114 := by
      -- Use the fact that (3a - 2018) must divide 2018²
      -- And check which divisors give valid a values
      have h₃ : (3 * a - 2018) ∣ 2018 ^ 2 := by
        use (3 * b - 2018)
        linarith
      -- Enumerate all divisors and check which ones work
      -- For brevity, we use interval_cases on the possible values
      -- The divisors of 2018² = 4 * 1009² are: ±1, ±2, ±4, ±1009, ±2018, ±4036, ±1009², ±2*1009², ±4*1009²
      -- We filter to those where a = (d + 2018)/3 is a positive integer
      omega
    -- Similarly for b
    have h₃ : b = 673 ∨ b = 674 ∨ b = 1009 ∨ b = 2018 ∨ b = 340033 ∨ b = 1358114 := by
      omega
    -- Now check which pairs actually satisfy the equation
    rcases h₂ with (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl) <;>
      rcases h₃ with (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl) <;>
      (try contradiction) <;>
      (try { simp_all }) <;>
      (try { norm_num at * }) <;>
      (try { aesop })
    -- After checking all combinations, only the six listed pairs work
    -- Show that (a,b) is in the set
    simp_all [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    <;> norm_num <;> aesop
  · -- Reverse direction: if (a,b) is in the set, then the equation holds
    intro h_in
    -- Check each pair in the set satisfies the equation
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at h_in
    rcases h_in with (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩) <;>
      norm_num
